Here's how.

AI can do a lot now. What I bring, as a human, is the way I see things, the way I listen, and the way I connect ideas and tell a story.

Seeing

Everyone's looking at the same thing, from the same angle.

When everyone works from the same references, the ideas start to look alike. Same campaigns, same posts, same pitches, and nothing stands out.

I can help you:

  • Find a fresh angle for your brand, product or campaign
  • Come up with ideas when you're stuck
  • Turn your numbers into a story people understand
  • Ideation
  • Campaign concepts
  • Product experience
  • Data storytelling

Listening

People rarely say what they really mean.

Customers tell you what they think you want to hear. Teams jump to a fix before they know the real problem. And across cultures, the same words can mean different things.

I can help you:

  • Understand your customers and what they actually want
  • Talk to people across cultures
  • Figure out the real problem before jumping to a solution
  • Customer insight
  • Cross-cultural communication
  • Research

Speaking

A good idea in the wrong words gets ignored.

Stiff copy, jargon, or a story that takes too long to start, and people scroll past. It doesn't matter how good the idea is if it doesn't sound human.

I can help you:

  • Tell your brand's story in a way that sounds human
  • Write for your website, social media and emails
  • Build a simple website to put it all in one place
  • Storytelling
  • Copywriting
  • Content
  • WordPress and Framer

If any of this sounds like something you need, I'd love to hear about it. Send me an email.

  1. 1Lead Storyteller at Good CupBlogs, captions and campaign ideas for a specialty coffee roastery.Storytelling

    I'm the voice behind the blogs and the captions for most posts. Ideation is part of everyone's job on the team, and I contribute ideas for social media and for campaigns.

  2. 2Designing with AI3D-printed keychains with NFC tags inside, like the octopus that links to this site.AI + 3D printing

    AI lets me try more ideas and build things I couldn't on my own, but it's a tool. The ideas, the choices and the final say are mine.

    Keychain Studio has a few keys. It also has three octopus keychains for 3D printing: see no evil, hear no evil and speak no evil.

    I built the studio with AI, so I could try more colors and finishes and see how each one would look before printing. AI also helped me make the files to send to the 3D printer.

    They’re not just for show. Each keychain has an NFC tag inside, so a phone can read it with a tap. The octopuses on this site are printed keychains too, and tapping one opens this website, which I also built with Claude. That took many rounds of back and forth. Claude helped shape it, but the judgment, the taste and knowing what feels right to a person came from me. Built online, made real offline.

    Tap one to wake it, drag to turn it around.

    It started with a visual idea: the octopuses turning gray. That reminded me of the Ibong Adarna, whose songs put you to sleep before it turns you to stone. That’s where Pedro, Diego and Juan got their names, from the three princes in the story.

    Why octopuses? I find them fascinating. They have three hearts, blue blood and nine brains. They're so different, and that resonates with me. I've never really felt like I belonged anywhere, not even in my own family. That's not meant to sound dramatic. It's just the feeling of being different.

  6. 6Feelings CoffeeA coffee brand I built from scratch: brand, packaging, sourcing and operations.Brand building

    It started during the lockdown. The original idea was closer to Leafly than to the sampler box it turned into.

    I was talking to one of my Tagalog students at the time, who was well-versed in startups. It was through him that I learned of Y Combinator. He was the first person who believed in the idea. “Your idea has bones,” he said.

    This was during the final leg of my MBA, when the last exam was cancelled because of the pandemic. In school, problems came as case studies: something that had already happened to some big company and was contained in classroom discussions. The risk stayed inside the controlled environment of a university, where you either pass or you fail.

    Feelings Coffee, on the other hand, was my first tiny (microscopic, really) attempt at business. It was happening live, and I was the one accountable for making the calls on marketing, packaging, operations, finance, logistics, sourcing and every problem in between. Unlike the case studies, the consequences were unknown. My decisions had more weight.

    In the beginning, it was all me. Eventually, I brought in an illustrator, architect and artist, who happened to be my sister. Working with her taught me that managing people well is a skill of its own. I learned that delegation and communication are key to running a business. And with customers, I learned that you can't read people's minds, so you have to listen.

    Feelings Coffee was an exercise in grit and perseverance.

    The boxes still live on Instagram.

    • Brand building

  7. 7Emirates Cabin CrewMore than four years working with crew from all over the world.Hospitality

    It's impossible to fit my adventures in one paragraph. But if we had met on one of the flights, our conversation would have probably started with, “Chicken or beef?”

    Back then, planes were like a hop-on, hop-off bus. I rarely flew with the same person twice. And my colleagues and passengers were from different parts of the world. That's where I learned to read people.

    • Cross-cultural communication
    • Service
    • Reading people
